newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia mobile phone monopoly illegal - court.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia mobile phone monopoly illegal - court.

text.p: Slovenia's Constitutional Court said on Wednesday it had ruled that state-owned Mobitel's mobile telephone network monopoly was unconstitutional.
The court said its verdict, reached on July 10, was based on the view that mobile telephony should be provided via the market and not as a public service.
"The monopoly was given to Mobitel without legal basis," it said in a statement.
Mobitel is currently the only Slovenian mobile telephone network operator holding a 10-year state licence to use radio frequencies. Other operators are only able to get short-term, trial licences.
"The court decided other companies should be given permission to use radio frequencies before next June, under the same conditions as Mobitel," said court secretary Janez Cebulj.
According to Slovenian telecommunication law, the government must annnounce a public tender for further concessions in the sector by the end of June 1998.
So far three companies -- Digitel, Detel 5 and consortium GSM -- have said they would like to operate in Slovenia's mobile telecommunications sector.
